questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
questions.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{t}^{2}-12t,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-12t) \\  & =6t-12\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1,$ the velocity is

$$
v(1)=6(1)-12=-6.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-6|=6.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity of a Particle at a Particular Moment
questions.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
s(t)={t}^{2}-2t+\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=3.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t+\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\  & =2t-2+\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =2(3)-2+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =6-2+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{13}{3} \\  & =4.333\,333… \\  & ≈4.33\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
questions.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in feet) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{e}^{-t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3t,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=3\,\text{s}.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{e}^{-t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3t) \\  & =-3{e}^{-t}+\frac{3}{t}-3\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=3,$ the velocity is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =-3{e}^{-3}+\frac{3}{3}-3 \\  & =-3{e}^{-3}-2 \\  & ≈-2.15\,\text{ft/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-2.15|=2.15\,\text{ft/s}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity of a Particle
questions.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1).$ Calculate the velocity at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot 2t \\  & =\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

s(t)=3{log}_{2}⁡t-2t,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=2.$ Round your answer to one decimal place.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{3}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-2 \\  & =0.16404… \\  & ≈0.2\end{aligned}
$$
